tagline: Your personal finances, at a glance.

auth.title: Sign in to Yield
auth.description: Your spending, cards, and income, all in one place.
auth.failed: Couldn't sign in. Please try again.

month.methodFromHere: Applies to this month and later ones; earlier months keep their method.
month.confirmDeletePurchase: Delete this purchase? Installment purchases are deleted from every month.
month.outstandingEmpty: Everything due this month is paid.

income.title: Income
income.empty: No income recorded this month yet.

add.expectedHint: A later date makes this expected: it shows in your forecast, and counts as received only once you confirm it on the day.
add.stillExpectedHint: Still expected: confirm it from the month view once it arrives.
add.plannedHint: A later date makes this a plan: it shows in your forecast, and leaves your cash only once you confirm it on the day.
add.stillPlannedHint: Still a plan: confirm it from the month view once it's spent.
add.exchangeHint: Moves money between your cash wallets at the rate you got. It isn't spending or income.
add.sourceExists: Already a source; this income goes to {name}.

settings.addWallet: Add a wallet in another currency
settings.confirmArchiveWallet: Archive this wallet? Its records keep it; it just won't be offered for new ones.
settings.currencyHint: Every figure is in this currency. Records in other currencies (like spending in dollars) are shown on their own; money on hand and savings in them count at today's exchange rate.
settings.incomeGroupsHint: Group sources to see their net income, like Rideshare (Uber, Didi) after Car spending.
settings.confirmArchiveGroup: Archive this group? Its sources keep their history and net; new sources can't join it.
settings.historyStartHint: Averages and typical daily spending skip earlier months, for when your first months only have some records (like card payments).
settings.cashOnHandHint: Cash, debit, and app balances, outside savings. It follows your income, cash spending, paid bills and statements, and savings from here; count it again whenever it drifts from your accounts.
settings.balanceGoalHint: What you want left over each month. Money moved into savings is still yours, so it never lowers your balance.
settings.title: Settings
settings.confirmRemove: Remove this from your lists? Past records keep it.
settings.paymentDaysHint: The payment is due this many days after the statement closes.
settings.incomeRhythmHint: When your income arrives. Needed per payday and Income per payday count these paydays; you still record each income as it comes.
settings.rhythmAnchorHint: Any past or upcoming payday; the rest follow from it.
settings.rhythmDaysHint: Days of the month, separated by commas. A day past the month’s end falls on its last day.
settings.moneyHint: Cash on hand and credit cards
settings.planningHint: Balance goal, income rhythm, and summaries
settings.cardsHint: Each card’s statements and upcoming installments
settings.sourcesHint: Where income comes from, and net by group
settings.recurringIncomeHint: Income on a schedule, like a salary
settings.estimatesHint: Rough amounts that stand in for your averages until you have a month of records, fading out as they come in. Leave any blank to drop it.
settings.estimatesDone: You have a month of records, so your averages no longer use these.

errors.walletExists: There's already a wallet in this currency.
errors.amount: Enter an amount greater than zero, with up to two decimals.
errors.installments: Installments must be a whole number from 1 to 48, and only apply to cards.
errors.name: Add a name.
errors.generic: Something went wrong. Please try again.
errors.coverMonths: Use a whole number of months from 1 to 24.
errors.recurringEnded: This recurring payment has ended and can't be edited.
errors.item: Choose an item or type a new one.
errors.itemExists: Another item already has this name. Merge them instead.
errors.paymentDays: Use a whole number of days from 1 to 60.
errors.payDays: Use days from 1 to 31, separated by commas (up to 8).
errors.rate: Enter a rate between 0 and 100%, like 15 or 8.5.

recurring.inCurrency: This bill is in {currency}: its amount stays in that currency, and it's paid from that wallet.
recurring.title: Recurring payments
recurring.description: Bills that repeat every month. They appear in each month to mark as paid; card-paid bills are paid with their card statement.
recurring.confirmStop: Stop this recurring payment? It stays in months already paid.
recurring.variableHint: Each month starts as an estimate from your recent bills; confirm the real amount when it arrives.
recurring.intervalHint: For bills every few months, start in a month that has a bill.
recurring.editHint: Changes apply from this month on; earlier months keep their amounts.
recurring.incomeDescription: Income that arrives on a schedule, like a salary. Each payday counts as expected in its month, and in the projected balance, until you mark it received.
recurring.firstPaydayHint: Any payday; the rest follow from it. A future date starts it then.
recurring.confirmStopIncome: Stop this recurring income? Income already received stays recorded.
recurring.incomeEditHint: Changes apply to paydays not received yet. A new schedule counts from today.

cards.title: Cards
cards.empty: Add your credit cards in Settings to track statements.

year.title: Year
year.noMonths: No months of this year count yet: they haven't started, or come before "Count history from" in Settings.
year.countedNote: Counts this year's months that have started, from "Count history from" in Settings on, since earlier months may hold only some records.
year.aboutBalance: What the year has left you so far: each month's income minus everything paid out that month, added up.
year.aboutIncome: Everything received in the year's months so far.
year.aboutToPay: Money that left in the year's months so far: cash purchases and bills, and card statements.
year.aboutSpending: What you bought in the year's months so far: purchases, installments, and recurring bills.
year.aboutSaved: Money moved into savings, less what was taken out, in the year's months so far. It's kept, not spent, so it never lowers the balance.
year.aboutAverageBalance: What a typical month of this year has left you: the year's balance divided by the months counted.
year.aboutBestMonth: The month of this year with the highest balance so far.

savings.title: Savings
savings.averageEmpty: Record a few months of spending to calculate your average.
savings.confirmArchiveGoal: Archive this goal? Its movements stay in your history.
savings.workCostsOut: Left out as work costs (your income groups deduct them): they stop if the income stops.
savings.excludedNote: Categories set to not count in the average (like Extras) are left out.
savings.rateHint: Optional. If the rate is a promotion, the day it ends and the rate after it; the forecast switches on that day.
savings.depositHint: Optional. The forecast moves it from your cash into this fund on its days. Record the actual deposit when you make it.
savings.earning: {rate}% a year · about {daily} a day, {monthly} a month

manage.kindHintEVERYDAY: Day-to-day spending, like food or gas: counts in daily net, needed per day, and averages.
manage.kindHintBILLS: Regular bills, like rent: counts in averages, but not in daily figures.
manage.kindHintOCCASIONAL: One-off spending, like Extras: left out of averages and daily figures.
manage.builtInNameHint: Leave empty to keep the default name.
manage.confirmArchiveCategory: Archive this category? Its items and history stay; it just won't be offered for new entries.
manage.itemsDescription: Reusable expenses grouped by category. Moving an item moves its whole history.
manage.moveHint: Moving an item to another category moves all its history.
manage.confirmMerge: Merge “{source}” into “{target}”? All its entries and recurring payments move to “{target}” and “{source}” is removed.
manage.confirmArchiveItem: Archive this item? Its history stays; typing its name again brings it back.
manage.itemsEmpty: No items yet. They're created when you record an expense.

summary.headline: Headline
summary.statsHint: Shown two per row, in this order.
summary.empty: No stats on this card yet.
summary.hiddenHint: Some stats only show when they apply, like deductions with an income group or a group’s figures when you also have other income.
summary.aboutAverage: What you usually spend per day, week or month.
summary.aboutAverageOf: What you usually spend on {what} per {period}, from your recent spending, with what you've spent so far in the current one below it (yellow once it's past the usual).
summary.everydayNote: Everyday spending is purchases in your everyday categories, as in a typical day.
summary.fullAmountsNote: Purchases count in full on the day you made them. Only finished days count toward the usual, from the last few full months.
summary.aboutSpendingOn: What you spent on {what} this month: purchases, installments due this month, and recurring bills.
summary.spendingOnNote: Counted as in the month's spending: card purchases included, and installments in the months they're due.

aboutIncomeOfFrame.week: {what} received this week, from Monday on.

summary.currentMonthOnly: Today and this week only apply to the current month.
summary.aboutAverageIncome: What {what} usually comes to per {period}, from your recent income, with what's come in so far in the current one below it (green once it reaches the usual).
summary.historyNote: Only finished days count toward the usual, from the last few full months (or since "Count history from").

averageSpending.title: Average spending
averageSpending.hint: What you usually spend on something per day, week, or month.

spending.title: Spending
spending.hint: This month's spending on everything, a category, or an item.

income.title: Income
income.hint: Income today, this week, or this month, from all income, a group, or a source.

averageIncome.title: Average income
averageIncome.hint: What you usually earn per day worked, day, week, or month.

explain.rareNote: Big things you buy rarely, like {items}, count spread over {months} months, not as if they came back every few weeks.
explain.expectedInPace: Pace the expected payments take the place of
explain.expectedInPaceNote: Expected payments from a source your pace already counts take the place of that source's share of the pace on their day, so it isn't counted twice.
explain.plannedInEveryday: Planned everyday purchases an average day covers
explain.plannedInEverydayNote: Everyday purchases planned for the days ahead count in full in the total to pay, so the average day they fall on only adds what's left of it.
explain.convertedAt: Other currencies count at the reference rate of {date} (European Central Bank), and change with it.
explain.savingsConverted: Funds in other currencies count at today's reference rate (European Central Bank).
explain.aboutBalance: What the month leaves you: its income minus everything paid out this month (Money out).
explain.aboutTotalIncome: Everything received this month, and on how many days.
explain.aboutSpending: What you bought this month: purchases (card ones included), installments due this month, and recurring bills.
explain.aboutToPay: Money leaving this month: cash purchases and bills, and card statements that close this month. Money moved into savings isn't spent, so it stays out.
explain.aboutOutstanding: What's still unpaid of this month's cash bills and card statements, plus cash purchases planned and not confirmed yet.
explain.aboutNeededPerDay: Income needed on each day left this month to cover what's still to pay, plus a typical day's everyday spending.
explain.aboutNeededPerDayGoal: Income needed on each day left this month to reach your balance goal, plus a typical day's everyday spending.
explain.aboutDailyIncome: Income per day this month over the days that have finished (today counts once it's over), days off included.
explain.aboutDaysOff: Days you can still take off this month at your recent pace of work and still cover the month.
explain.aboutDaysOffGoal: Days you can still take off this month at your recent pace of work and still reach your balance goal.
explain.aboutProjectedBalance: Where the month's balance is headed if income and everyday spending keep their recent pace.
explain.aboutExpectedIncome: Income not received yet this month: recurring paydays and payments you're expecting.
explain.aboutNeededPerPayday: Income needed on each payday left this month to cover what's still to pay and everyday spending until the month ends.
explain.aboutNeededPerPaydayGoal: Income needed on each payday left this month to reach your balance goal, with everyday spending until the month ends.
explain.aboutIncomePerPayday: Average income per payday so far this month.
explain.aboutDeductions: Spending in the categories your income groups deduct: the costs of earning that income, like gas.
explain.aboutSavings: Money in your savings funds right now, whatever the month, and how far it is from their goals. The emergency fund's goal is months of average spending plus installments owed, as on the Savings page.
explain.aboutCashOnHand: Money you have right now (cash, debit, and app balances, outside savings): your last count in Settings, moved by what you've recorded since.
explain.noSavings: Add a deposit on the Savings page to start tracking it.
explain.savingsKept: Moving money into savings lowers cash on hand, never the balance: it's kept, not spent.
explain.noRateYet: There's no exchange rate yet for {amounts}, so it isn't added in.
explain.otherCurrencies: Amounts in other currencies are never converted or added in: {amounts}.
explain.noIncome: No income recorded this month yet.
explain.noGoal: Set a monthly balance goal in Settings to see how close you are to it.
explain.goalSavings: Moving money into savings isn't spending, so it never lowers the balance.
explain.spendingCards: Card purchases count here on the day you make them; their statement pays them later, in Money out.
explain.toPayCards: Card purchases count only through their statement, so nothing is counted twice.
explain.carried: Bills and statements from earlier months that are still unpaid count in their own month's totals, so they're shown beside this one, not in it.
explain.monthEnded: This month has ended, so there are no days left to count.
explain.everydayNote: Everyday spending per day is your purchases in everyday categories over the last {days} finished days (today counts once it's over), divided by them. Recurring bills and installments of earlier purchases aren't included.
explain.everydaySoFarNote: Everyday spending counts purchases in everyday categories, without recurring bills or installments of earlier purchases.
explain.breakEvenPerDay: Without the goal, {amount} a day covers the month.
explain.breakEvenPerPayday: Without the goal, {amount} per payday covers the month.
explain.covered: It's zero once the month is covered.
explain.dailyTarget: Green once it reaches the day's target of {amount} (Needed per day).
explain.paydayTarget: Green once it reaches the payday's target of {amount} (Needed per payday).
explain.daysOffPace: Your recent pace: {workDays} days worked in the last {days} finished days (today counts once it's over), each leaving {amount} after the costs of working (spending in the categories your income groups deduct, like gas).
explain.livingNote: Living costs are everyday spending per day without those categories, since a day off doesn't spend them.
explain.daysOffBreakEvenNote: Without the goal, {count} days off still cover the month.
explain.moreWorkThanDays: More work days are needed than there are days left, so none are off.
explain.daysOffNoPace: Shown once there's income in the last {days} finished days (today counts once it's over) and a day worked earns more than it costs.
explain.currentMonthOnly: Only counted for the current month.
explain.paceNote: The recent pace is your income over the last {days} finished days (today counts once it's over) divided by all of them, days off included. Recurring income is left out, since it's expected instead.
explain.expectedNote: A payday or expected payment stays expected until you mark it received in the month view; an expected payment whose day passes without that no longer counts as coming.
explain.noPaydaysLeft: No paydays are left this month, so the whole amount shows.
explain.rhythmNote: Paydays follow your income rhythm in Settings.
explain.beforeFirstPayday: Shown after the month's first payday.
explain.perDayWorked: Days without income aren't counted, unlike Month's daily income, which counts every day so far.
explain.cashNotCounted: Count what you have in Settings to start tracking it.
explain.cashCards: Card purchases leave it only when their statement is paid, and bills still pending aren't taken out.
explain.restOfTodayIncome: Rest of today at your recent pace
explain.restOfTodayNote: Today counts what you've recorded so far plus whatever an average day still has to bring in and spend, so it reads about the same whenever you log.
explain.workedTodayNote: Today has income, so it's a day worked rather than a day off; anything more you log today still lowers what's left to cover.
explain.estimateNote: While you have under a month of records, {percent}% of it is still your estimate of {amount} a month (your records alone: {real} a day).
explain.paceEstimateNote: While you have under a month of records, {percent}% of the pace is still your estimate of {amount} a month (your records alone: {real} a day).

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.hint: Each morning, a reminder of payments due in the next 3 days that aren't marked paid: cash bills and card statements, overdue ones included. Nothing is sent when nothing is due.
notifications.on: Reminders are on for this device.
notifications.testBody: You'll get a reminder in the morning when a payment is due soon.
notifications.unsupported: This browser can't receive notifications. On an iPhone, add Yield to your home screen first.
notifications.denied: Notifications are blocked for Yield. Allow them in your phone's settings, then try again.
notifications.notConfigured: Notifications aren't set up on the server yet.

forecast.howConverted: Money in other currencies counts at today's rate: {rates}.
forecast.title: Forecast
forecast.subtitle: Your cash on hand for the next {days} days, if income and spending keep their recent pace.
forecast.nothingUpcoming: No bills, statements or recurring income in the next three months.
forecast.how: It starts from your cash on hand and adds each day your recent income pace ({pace} a day) less your typical everyday cash spending ({spending} a day), from your last {days} days. Bills paid in cash fall on their due dates, and recurring income on its paydays.
forecast.howCards: Card spending leaves your cash when its statement is due: what's already on it (purchases, installments, card bills), plus the card's typical everyday spending for the days still to come in its cycle.
forecast.howFaded: Past {days} days the line is dashed: the further out, the rougher the guess, until more months of history firm it up.
forecast.spendingNote: Red bars are what leaves your cash each day: everyday spending, and bills and card statements on their dates.
forecast.needsCash: The forecast starts from your cash on hand. Count it in Settings to see where it's headed.
forecast.howSavings: The blue line adds your savings to your cash: what's in each fund now, the deposits you've planned, and the interest each fund earns, worked out daily at its rate and switching to the next rate when a promotional one ends. Planned deposits show in blue on top of that day's bar: they leave your cash, but they aren't spending.

onboarding.preview: Preview: nothing you enter here is saved.
onboarding.previewDone: End of the preview. Nothing was saved.
onboarding.skipAll: Skip setup, I'll do it later
onboarding.error: Something didn't save. Check your answers and try again.

welcome.note: Thanks for wanting to take better care of your money. I made Yield because I needed it for my own finances, saw how much it helped, and wanted to share it. It's a personal project and still in development, so you may run into rough edges or things that change. If anything is confusing, broken, or missing, tell me any time with "Send feedback" at the top. — Jorge
welcome.title: Where does your money go?
welcome.body: A few quick questions and Yield tells you how your month is going before it's over. First: what currency do you use?
welcome.currencyHint: You can log in other currencies too; this is the one your main figures use.

income.title: How does money come in?
income.body: A steady paycheck, gigs on the side, tips, commissions… or a bit of everything. This is how Yield knows what to expect, and when. Pick all that apply.
income.salaryHint: About the same amount on set days
income.variableHint: Freelance, commissions, sales, tips, rideshare… you log it as it comes in
income.invalid: Check the name, the amount and the pay days.
income.estimate: Roughly how much does it bring in a month?
income.estimateHint: Optional. So your first numbers don't start at zero.

cash.title: How much do you have right now?
cash.body: Cash, debit and apps, not savings or credit cards. It's your starting line for knowing whether you'll make it to the end of the month, and with how much.

cards.title: Do you use credit cards?
cards.body: Cards are sneaky: you buy today, but the money leaves when the bill is due. Yield keeps track of every statement so a due date never catches you off guard.
cards.name: Card name
cards.invalid: Each card needs a name, a closing day (1–31) and days to pay (1–60).

bills.title: What you pay every month, no matter what
bills.body: Rent, power, internet, the gym you swear you'll start going to… Add them once and Yield shows you when they're coming and what you need to cover them.
bills.variableHint: Changes month to month: enter about how much.
bills.invalid: Each bill needs a name, an amount and a day (1–31), and names can't repeat.

categories.title: Where does it all go?
categories.body: The daily coffee? Weekend plans? Groceries? Categories are the buckets your spending falls into, like Food or Transport. Inside go items, the actual things you buy: Tacos or Groceries inside Food. Items get created as you log, so for now just pick your categories.
categories.estimateIntro: Optional: how much do you think you spend a month on each? A guess is fine. We'll use it while your real numbers come in, and in a few weeks we'll show you how close you were (spoiler: almost nobody gets it right).
categories.estimateFor: About how much a month on {category}
categories.structural: Your bills go in Fixed, and one-off purchases that shouldn't count toward your averages go in Extras. Both are already set up, so no need to add them here. You can change all of this later in Settings.
categories.invalid: Each category needs a name, and names can't repeat.
categories.invalidEstimate: Enter amounts like 4,000, or leave them blank.

done.title: You're set. Now let's see where it goes.
done.body: Log what you spend and earn as it happens with the + button; it takes five seconds. Your numbers start out as rough estimates and get sharper with every week you log.
done.variable: Income logged as it comes in
done.nothing: Nothing set up yet. That's fine: you can do it all from Settings.

setup.title: Finish setting up
setup.cards: Add your credit cards, if you use any

estimates.title: How close were you?
estimates.body: Your guesses against your first {days} days.

account.title: Delete my account
account.hint: Erase your account and all your data
account.body: This erases your account and everything in it, for good: your spending, income, bills, cards, savings and settings. It can't be undone.
account.deleted: Your account and all its data were deleted. Thanks for trying Yield.

feedback.title: Send feedback
feedback.settingsHint: Ideas, bugs, or anything that feels off
feedback.intro: Yield is a personal project I'm building in my spare time, and it's still in beta. What you tell me shapes what comes next.
feedback.introAsk: Something confusing, a figure that looks wrong, an idea, or just what you like: all of it helps. I read every message.
feedback.placeholder: What happened, or what would make Yield better for you?
feedback.thanksBody: Your message reached me. If it needs an answer, I'll write to your account's email.
feedback.tooMany: That's a lot of messages for one day. Try again tomorrow, or email me.
feedback.notificationBody: Someone sent feedback on Yield. Tap to read it.
